title: ASCII Kinesis V2 Locomotion 023 — Narrow Support / Tandem Thread / Runout

source.identity: The Prince — Prince of Persia — Sega Genesis — Playable Characters
observed: The commissioned evidence explicitly inspected the full 552×1104 static sprite sheet as one locomotion corpus.
Large body travel is bracketed by support changes; grounded, airborne, low/compressed, recovery, and edge-contact families are all present.
The static sheet supplies no reliable source-authentic exposure durations.
unknown: Source-authentic chronology, exposure duration, gameplay cadence, root coordinates, support-force magnitudes, and any narrow-support-lane choreography are unknown.

rights.output_description: independent generic plan-view ASCII biped/root-support rig negotiating an authored narrowing support corridor

novelty.new_causality: Forward travel survives a support-width collapse. COM recenters before the feet enter a narrow support corridor; support ownership then advances through deliberately tandem foot placements while root motion remains live. When the corridor releases, the first free catch becomes overlong and laterally wide, then shorter correction steps pay width-rebound and torso-lag debt.
failure_if: COM does not center before the first narrow-lane catch
feet remain wide or teleport across the narrow lane
root travel halts while support width collapses
tandem threading becomes a symmetric generic gait
first free catch is not visibly longer/wider than constrained steps
corrections do not shorten after the free overrun
recovery snaps to idle or erases torso lag

timing.playback_policy: authored decisive causal keys with explicit holds; deterministic connective labor may not invent support/contact/root decisions; no reverse interpolation

rig.support_rule: A support owner remains world-fixed through its pass/unload state. The authored constraint changes the allowed lateral support width, not the existence of ground. Narrow-lane catches must land inside the corridor and transfer in order.
rig.constraint_rule: COM approaches the lane centerline before the first constrained foot placement. Through K06-K10 foot separation remains roughly tandem; root x travel remains positive. After K11 the corridor opens and K12 deliberately overshoots width and forward spacing before shorter corrections.
rig.recovery_rule: K12 is the largest post-constraint spacing event; K13-K15 progressively reduce forward debt while torso yaw and COM lateral offset settle asymmetrically without returning to idle.

tango.inspection: The support corridor visibly narrows before entry, COM recenters by K03 before the first constrained catch, world-fixed supports hand off inside the narrow lane without halting root travel, K06-K10 compress to tandem placements and short spacing, then K12 releases into a visibly overlong/wider free catch followed by shorter K13-K15 corrections with torso lag and displaced recovery.

noodle_queen.inspection: The corridor is not decorative: the feet actually narrow into it while the root keeps traveling, then the exit snaps open into one memorable overlong catch and a shrinking correction tail. The specimen stays specific, causal, asymmetric, and does not reset to idle.
